messages.author: 9d0b6fd7d62aa252
messages.subject: Mesh creation using use “fmesher::fm_mesh_2d_inla()”function
parts:
Hi,

Yesterday, I raised a concern about mesh creation, and you suggested using "fmesher::fm_mesh_2d_inla()." I've now utilized this function to generate a mesh, which I intend to employ in a spatio-temporal analysis with the INLA model. However, I've observed that the process of mesh creation is exceedingly time-consuming. In fact, I initiated it yesterday and allowed it to run overnight, but it's still ongoing. I'm wondering whether the arguments I've used in the "fm_mesh_2d_inla()" function, such as "max.edge" and "min.angle," are affecting the time it takes to create the mesh, or if the extended duration is due to limitations in my computer hardware.

These are some of the codes i am using

library (INLA)
library (fields)
library(readr)
library(sp)
library(fmesher)
memory.limit ()
memory . limit ( size =211631800000)
setwd("D:/ DATASETs")
borders <- read.csv("amhara region border.csv ")
head(borders)
index <- dim(borders)[1]
plot(borders)
BB1=borders[borders$X<320000 & borders$X>300000 & borders$Y<1350000 & borders$Y>1250000,]
BB=borders[-c(2875:2906),]
plot(BB,type="l",lwd=3)
coordinates <- read.csv("coordinates.csv")
head(coordinates)
coordinates_val <- read.csv("coordinates_Val.csv")
head(coordinates_val )
data <- read.csv("infectedrate weekly.csv")
head(data)
str(data)
data_val <- read.csv("infectedrate_val_weekly.csv")
head(data_val)
str(data_val)
n_stations = length(coordinates$ID)
n_stations_val = length(coordinates_val$ID)
n_data = length(data$ID)
n_data_val = length(data_val$ID )
n_days = as.integer(n_data/n_stations)
n_days_val = as.integer(n_data_val/n_stations_val )
mean_covariates = apply(data[,5:17],2,mean )
sd_covariates = apply(data[,5:17],2,sd)
data[,5:17] = scale(data[,5:17], mean_covariates,sd_covariates)
mean_covariates_val = apply (data_val[,5:17],2,mean)
sd_covariates_val = apply(data_val[,5:17],2,sd)
data_val[,5:17] = scale(data_val[,5:17],mean_covariates_val,sd_covariates_val)
data$loginfected = log(data$Infected.rate)
data_val$loginfected = log(data_val$infectedrate_val)
data$time = rep(1:n_days, each = n_stations)
data_val$time = rep(1:n_days_val, each = n_stations_val)
loc1=SpatialPoints(as.matrix(cbind(coordinates$X,coordinates$Y)))
loc2=SpatialPoints(BB)
borders2=rbind(BB,coordinates[,3:4])
loc3=SpatialPoints(borders2)
mesh = fmesher::fm_mesh_2d_inla(loc = cbind ( coordinates $X , coordinates $Y )
                                ,loc.domain = loc3, offset =c(10, 140),max.edge =c(50,1000) ,min.angle=c(27,21))

I would greatly appreciate your assistance in resolving this matter.

Thank you in advance.

Regards,
Flavian

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Mesh creation using use “fmesher::fm_mesh_2d_inla()”function
parts:
Hi,
first of all, check your coordinate units and make sure the offset and
max.edge values are reasonable. I'm guessing your coordinates are in
metres? Then it depends on the size of your domain what values are
reasonable, but I suspect that offset 10 is much too small; Normally,
the offset would be _larger_ than max.edge, not smaller.
Also, please try with min.angle=21, to make sure that's not the issue;
21 is the largest value for which the algorithm is guaranteed to
terminate.

Also set the max.n.strict and max.n arguments to limit the allowed
total number of mesh vertices (set e.g. to 10000). This should cause
it to stop after adding too many points. That way, if it _still_ takes
a long time to run, we'll know there's some other problem.

Finn
